description: Chrome proportion shrink-only ratchet baseline (tempdoc 697). ONE authority for the per-ui-shot-step persistent-chrome elements whose rendered HEIGHT must not GROW beyond a recorded ceiling (maxHeightPx). Shrinking is always allowed; growth beyond maxHeightPx + tolerancePx is a violation, enforced by `jseval ui-proportion-gate` (which reuses the ui-shot `.measure.json` geometry — see scripts/jseval/jseval/ui_measure.py). Regenerate via scripts/jseval/experiments/regen_proportion_baseline.py. ACTIVE (tempdoc 697 activation): both target elements were DATA-DEPENDENT (a degraded readiness verdict for the collapsed pill; a rendered turn for the one-line user bubble) and are now captured deterministically by the dedicated isolated `chat-proportion` ui-shot step (scripts/jseval/jseval/ui_check.py), which installs the `degraded` fixtures variant (ui_fixtures._status_body — flips `readiness.composites.retrieval` to DEGRADED with `worker.health.embedding_not_ready`, a 'warn'-severity LifecycleReasonCode so the banner renders collapsed) and actually submits a chat turn (a `?`-bearing draft + Enter, escalating to UnifiedChatView.send()). `chat-mode` (the shared chain step) is untouched — it documents chat-INPUT mode only and never submits, so it was not repurposed. Both elements' `maxHeightPx` were filled in by regen_proportion_baseline.py from this step's live `--fixtures` capture; with the top-level `tolerancePx` of 2px folded in, the effective ceilings are 44px (pill) and 38px (bubble).
captureState: ui-shot --fixtures (deterministic); the `chat-proportion` isolated step (degraded status fixture + a submitted chat turn) — see tempdoc 697; the `chat-occlusion` isolated step (1250x800, document pane opened, a toast burst at exactly the cap) — see below. The 814 closure adds `chat-bands-detailed`: the same band family in DETAILED disclosure (the `degraded-detailed` fixtures variant — identical to `degraded` except it does NOT flip `ui.mode` to simple, so the app boots into Advanced and the banner force-expands) at 1366x900, ABOVE the 820px block-axis breakpoint so Detailed genuinely expands, with one overflowing user turn so the conversation actually scrolls. Round 8 moved that step from 1050x800 to 1250x800: the wide breakpoint became a `@container` query on the chat SURFACE box (viewport minus the Shell rail minus the surface padding), so 1050 no longer mounts the wide grid at all and `.document-pane` would leave the capture; 1250 gives the surface ~1042px, the same just-over-1024 worst case the original width was reaching for. The `tasks-occlusion` isolated step (tempdoc 813 Slice D) captures at 1280x800 with the `indexing` fixtures variant (ui_fixtures._status_body: a live INDEXING worker with a real backlog), which is what puts the Tasks panel's aggregate card on screen — under every other fixture the worker reports the fallback state "SERVING", which the progress projection refuses to read, so the panel is correctly invisible.
constraintKinds: An element declares at least one of: `maxHeightPx` (shrink-only chrome ratchet, tempdoc 697); `minHeightPx` (the 814 review pass's anti-vacuity FLOOR companion to a ceiling — a band registered because it EXPANDS must not pass its ceiling by collapsing: `.degradation-banner`'s 176px Detailed ceiling was satisfied at the 34px collapsed pill, i.e. precisely in the regression the row exists to catch; same move as `minScrollableRegions` beside `maxScrollableRegions`); `minWidthPx` (a FLOOR for primary content that surrounding chrome must not starve); `mustNotOverlapSelector` (two rects must not intersect — occlusion, which no per-element size budget can express); `minShareOfSelector` (tempdoc 814 D1/D7.1 — this element's rect.h / a named denominator selector's rect.h must be >= floor, the 'owner of the sum' share assertion); `maxBottomPx` (tempdoc 814 D6/D7.2, the F5 close — rect.y + rect.h must stay within a pinned viewport height). A STEP may also declare `maxScrollableRegions` (tempdoc 814 D3/D7.2 — geometry.scrollableCount must not exceed this) and/or `minScrollableRegions` (the 814 closure audit's finding C — the anti-vacuity FLOOR: a ceiling alone passes trivially on a capture with zero scrollers, so a step whose state is supposed to overflow declares the floor too; the pair 1/1 is what makes the one-scroller rule witness a real scroller) and/or `statusFactsSingleton: true` (tempdoc 814 D5/D7.3 — every governance/status-facts.v1.json phrase must not exceed its registered maxPersistentRenders) and/or `absentSelectors` (a selector that must NOT appear in the captured geometry) and/or `requiredSelectors` (its positive twin — a selector that MUST appear; the spine pair's positive half) and/or `forbiddenVisibleText` (814 D5 review pass — literal phrases that must not render VISIBLY in this step's state, counted by the same visibility-filtered statusFacts probe with a step-scoped ceiling of 0; the chip-yield witness, which the register-wide phrase counter structurally cannot be because that duplication is cross-worded). Enforced by `jseval ui-proportion-gate`; an element with no constraint, or a selector missing from the captured geometry, is an ERROR, never a silent pass.
occlusionNote: Sandbox round 7 registered two layout defects on the `chat-occlusion` capture. (1) `.conversation` — the RAG reading column measured 102px wide (about one word per line) at 1050x800 with the document pane open, because CONVERSATION_ZONES declared its grid track `minmax(0, 50rem)` while its neighbours reserved real min-widths; the track floor is now 24rem, so the floor here is 384px. (2) `.toast` vs `.header` — the OverlayHost `.top-right` column docked at 48px, inside the chat surface's 56-88px header band, completely covering the shape badge; the dock now clears the surface header row as well as the topbar. Round 8 then showed the dock offset alone was not enough for the toast column: a `REQUIRES_ACK` toast had NO timeout, so two of them were still covering the Library header's control row ~6 minutes and several navigations later. That is fixed at the toast, not at the slot — every toast is now time-bounded (AdvisoryToastHost's TOAST_DURATION_MS / ACK_TOAST_DURATION_MS), the record keeping its durable home in the advisory inbox drawer + rail badge. HONEST RESIDUAL: the `top: calc(2.5rem + 3rem + 0.5rem)` reservation is calibrated against the CHAT surface's header band (measured y 56-88) and does NOT clear surfaces that stack a `<jf-surface-tabs>` strip above their own header — Library's header band ends at y=143 against chat's y=89, so the slot's persistent occupants (jf-provenance-badge, jf-plugin-error-overlay) can still land on a Library-shaped header. A per-surface header offset, not a single global constant, is what would close it. (3) `jf-task-list` vs the rail's bottom controls — tempdoc 813 Slice D. The OverlayHost `.bottom-left` slot docked at `left: 1rem`, i.e. INSIDE the 3.25rem rail column, so the Tasks panel covered the Settings button and the Help affordance outright; the slot now reserves the rail's band via the `--rail-width` token Shell.ts lays its grid track out with, so the reservation follows rail expansion (11rem) instead of being calibrated to one state. Registered as TWO overlap rows (panel vs Settings, Help vs panel) plus a `minWidthPx: 140` floor on `jf-task-list` itself — the NON-VACUITY companion: a hidden element is still found by `ui_measure`'s deepQuery but yields a 0x0 rect, which satisfies `_rects_overlap` trivially, so without a size constraint the two overlap rows would report clean precisely when the panel failed to render. 140px is a deliberate FLOOR, not a measured width (the panel is content-sized under a 24rem cap; measured 159px at this step — the floor was lowered from 160, which passed only on the 2px tolerance). The pre-existing `.toast` row shares this latent vacuity and does NOT yet carry a companion — noted for Lane-2/T-B rather than fixed here.

steps.$comment: Tempdoc 814 D7.2's spine PAIR, positive half (landed in the 2026-08-06 review pass; W4 had deferred it as needing DOM changes that have since merged). Two user turns + the agent affordance MUST mount the spine — the regression `chat-spine-single`'s absence assertion cannot catch on its own (a spine that never mounts at all passes the negative row trivially). DIVISION: the capture witnesses PRESENCE; 'marker count == segment count' stays unit-tier (adaptiveSpacing / UnifiedChatView tests) because segmented nodeIds need a real agent SSE run, which `install_fixtures` stubs empty.

Tempdoc 814 D5's chip-yield CAPTURE witness (review pass 2026-08-06). The chip yield is a cross-worded duplication — the banner says 'Semantic search degraded.' and the chip 'Service degraded' — so the phrase-singleton register structurally cannot witness it; what a capture CAN decide is that the banner-owning surface never shows the chip's wording. This step reaches the degraded chat surface WITHOUT submitting, because a submitted turn leaves `aiState.activity` stuck on 'thinking' under --fixtures (the stubbed SSE never drains) and the chip then reads 'Thinking…' whether the yield works or not — measured on `chat-bands`: 'Thinking' 1, 'Service degraded' 0, a green for the wrong reason. `requiredSelectors` is the non-vacuity companion: the assertion only means something while the banner is the authority on screen.
